mandate: Helios owns the clock. It is the only specialist that judges WHEN a candidate is valid: it re-derives entry-window membership of the trigger candle's close from raw config (§1), independently recomputes the session-box label and cross-checks it against Snapshot.session (catching stale session.boxes config or session_of bugs), enforces the TIME half of the pre-09:30 rule by verifying the NY-VWAP family is null before its anchor (§3/architecture invariant 1), verifies temporal integrity of the snapshot payload (Snapshot.ts == Trigger.ts, no future-dated bar_ts or data-level event_time — a lookahead tripwire), classifies each data-level row as final vs still-developing against its N-minute formation window (§2), determines news-day status for the §6.3 override to the extent the Snapshot permits (honestly emitting "unknown" when later-today releases are invisible), computes the late-window-entry sizing flag (§9), and surfaces session-integrity anomalies (weekend/maintenance timestamps, suspected CME holidays/early closes, quarterly roll weeks) as auditable context for the human. Helios never judges price structure, cluster composition, candle anatomy, direction, or trade construction — it reads timestamps, nulls, and impact tags, not prices (data_high/data_low are deliberately outside its allowlist).
strategy_slice_refs: §1 (Instrument, Session, Timeframes — entry-window variants W1/W2/W3, entry TFs, EOD flatten context)
§2 rows: NY session VWAP (anchored 09:30, does NOT exist pre-market), Daily VWAP (18:00 ET anchor, the ONLY VWAP pre-9:30), Session boxes, Data levels (extremes within N min of releases)
§3 sentence: 'Pre-9:30, the VWAP family = daily VWAP only'
§6.3 (News-day override — high-impact data days, elevated sweep probability)
§7 news handling sentence (data is bias/target input, not blackout; H4 'no entry within N min of release' = test-only)
config_refs: sizing.late_window_min (PROPOSED — does not exist yet; see open questions)

checks.name: entry_window_validity
checks.pass_condition: Let t = wall-clock ET time of Trigger.ts (the candle CLOSE, parsed from the tz-aware ISO string — never offset arithmetic). Let (start, end) = session.entry_windows.{session.entry_window}.start/.end. If start < end (non-wrapping, e.g. W1): pass iff start <= t < end. If start > end (wrapping, e.g. W2 18:00→15:55): pass iff t >= start OR t < end. Otherwise fail.
checks.fail_note: Veto. Trigger closed outside the active entry window — either an engine filtering bug or a stale entry_window config. Note the engine/Vault must ALSO enforce this deterministically; Helios is the independent cross-check, never the sole enforcement.

checks.name: session_label_recompute
checks.pass_condition: Recompute the box label for Trigger.ts from raw config: for each box in session.boxes (in declared order), t is inside iff start <= t < end when start <= end, else (t >= start OR t < end); label = first matching box name, or "" if none (the 16:00–18:00 ET gap is legitimately ""). Pass iff recomputed label == Snapshot.session exactly (including the empty-string case).
checks.fail_note: Veto. Snapshot.session disagrees with an independent re-derivation from config — session_of bug or config drift; downstream session-extreme targets are suspect.

checks.name: timestamp_coherence
checks.rule_ref: §5.2 ('Candle must CLOSE to confirm') + architecture invariants 2–3 (tz-aware ET, closed candles / no-lookahead)
checks.pass_condition: ALL of: (a) Snapshot.ts == Trigger.ts == indicators.ts after ISO parse; (b) every non-null indicators.tfs.{1min,2min,3min,5min}.bar_ts <= Snapshot.ts (no future-stamped bar = lookahead tripwire); (c) for the trigger's own TF, 0 <= (Trigger.ts − indicators.tfs.{Trigger.tf}.bar_ts) <= one Trigger.tf period (tolerating the START-labeled 1min base frame), i.e. the trigger was evaluated on a just-closed candle, not stale data.
checks.fail_note: Veto. Snapshot and Trigger are temporally inconsistent or the trigger-TF bar is stale — a data gap at the trigger or a builder bug; nothing downstream can be trusted.

checks.name: premarket_vwap_time_regime
checks.rule_ref: §3 ('Pre-9:30, the VWAP family = daily VWAP only') + §2 NY VWAP row + architecture invariant 1
checks.pass_condition: Let t = ET time of Trigger.ts, anchor = indicators.ny_vwap.anchor. If t < anchor (pre-market): pass iff EVERY indicators.ny_vwap field (mid, upper_1..3, lower_1..3) is null AND indicators.daily_vwap.mid is non-null. If t >= anchor + one Trigger.tf period and t < 17:00 ET: pass iff indicators.ny_vwap.mid is non-null. In the grace interval [anchor, anchor + one Trigger.tf period): no ny_vwap requirement (first NY bar may not have closed). Also emit flags.premarket = (t < anchor).
checks.fail_note: Veto. NY VWAP leaking pre-market poisons cluster composition (Atlas independently checks the composition half — no cluster member named nyvwap_* pre-anchor; this is the deliberate dual-key). Null NY VWAP well after the open, or null daily VWAP, means broken indicators.

checks.name: data_level_availability
checks.rule_ref: §2 (data levels: extremes printed within N min of releases) + §6.3 input integrity
checks.pass_condition: Every data_levels[].event_time <= Snapshot.ts (a future-dated event in the snapshot = engine lookahead bug = FAIL). Additionally classify each row: developing iff event_time + indicators.data_levels.window_min > Snapshot.ts — its extreme is still forming and must be listed in flags.developing_data_levels[] (an output obligation, not a gate failure); rows with elapsed windows are final and usable as §6.3/§6 target inputs.
checks.fail_note: Veto on any future-dated event_time (lookahead). Developing rows never veto but MUST be flagged so Hephaestus/the human do not treat a half-formed data extreme as a final target level.

checks.name: news_day_classification
checks.pass_condition: Emit flags.news_day per this exact rule: 'high_impact' iff at least one data_levels row has impact == 'high' AND event_time falls in the current CME session (session date derived via the indicators.daily_vwap.anchor 18:00 ET boundary, matching engine grouping); otherwise 'unknown' — never 'normal', because the Snapshot carries only PAST events and a later-today high-impact release is invisible without an engine-provided news_context field. Gate passes iff the emitted value follows this derivation; any other value, or use of outside/world knowledge of the economic calendar, is a fail. Stale rows from prior sessions must be excluded from the classification.
checks.fail_note: Fail-closed on malformed output. 'unknown' does NOT veto — it is surfaced to Hermes/the human; whether unknown downgrades the §6.3 override is an Angus call (open question). The calendar file itself is engine input; Helios must never read files or supply calendar facts from memory.

checks.name: late_window_entry
checks.pass_condition: Compute minutes_to_window_close = (active window end − Trigger.ts) in wall-clock ET, wrap-aware for W2. Emit flags.late_window_entry = (minutes_to_window_close <= sizing.late_window_min). Gate = pass whenever the flag and minutes_to_window_close are computed and emitted; gate = fail only if inputs are missing/uncomputable (fail-closed). This is an ADVISORY sizing input, never a trade veto — §9 makes late-window a half-unit condition, not a skip.
inputs: config:sizing.late_window_min (PROPOSED — missing key, see open questions)
checks.fail_note: The flag feeds §9 half-unit sizing, which Helios does not apply — see split_concerns for who composes §9 (recommendation: Vault recomputes deterministically; Helios's flag is the cross-check).

checks.name: session_integrity
checks.rule_ref: §1 (session definition) + §12.2 (divergences audited) — weak § anchor, flagged for Angus; no constitution rule covers holidays/roll explicitly
checks.pass_condition: Hard gate (binary): ref_price is non-null AND Trigger.ts is NOT inside a known CME closed period (Saturday any time; Sunday before 18:00 ET; Friday at/after 17:00 ET; the 17:00–18:00 ET daily maintenance break) — a trigger stamped inside a closure is corrupt data. Advisory half (never fails the gate): populate flags.session_anomalies[] with any of — suspected CME full holiday or early close for the trigger date (LLM calendar knowledge, clearly labeled 'suspected — engine has no holiday input'); quarterly futures roll week (mid Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec); Snapshot.session == '' at trigger time; null session_high/session_low during an active session.
checks.fail_note: Hard half vetoes (data from a closed market is unusable). Advisory anomalies are for the human's audit trail only — the Snapshot carries no roll flag, holiday calendar, or gap statistics, so these are judgment-flagged suspicions, not verdicts (missing engine fields listed in open questions).

prompt_version.description: semver of .claude/agents/helios.md — prompt edits are versioned like code

verdict.description: AND of all gates; Hermes recomputes and treats any mismatch, missing field, or invalid JSON as fail (fail-closed)

late_window_entry.description: computability only — the substantive output is flags.late_window_entry

session_integrity.description: hard half only; advisory anomalies never fail this gate

premarket.description: Trigger.ts ET time < indicators.ny_vwap.anchor (§3 time half)

news_day.description: 'normal' is only emittable once the engine provides a forward-looking news_context Snapshot field; until then the derivation rule permits only high_impact|unknown

developing_data_levels.description: event names whose N-min formation window has not elapsed at Snapshot.ts

session_anomalies.description: advisory: suspected holiday/early close, roll week, session=='' at trigger, null session extremes

active_window.description: echo of config session.entry_window, e.g. W1

computed.description: shown work — lets Hermes and the human audit the arithmetic behind every gate

thesis.description: 2–3 sentence human-auditable time/session/news narrative, e.g. 'Trigger 09:42 ET, W1 window with 78 min remaining, NY session confirmed, CPI 08:30 high-impact extremes final and in play — news day.'

edge_cases: W2 wraps midnight (18:00 → 15:55): all window arithmetic must be wrap-aware — a 16:30 ET trigger is OUTSIDE W2 (after flatten, before reopen) even though 16:30 is 'between' the configured times numerically.

Boundary closes: a candle closing exactly at window start (08:00:00) or end (11:00:00). Recommend half-open [start, end) on the CLOSE timestamp; a 5min candle closing exactly 11:00 uses 10:55–11:00 data — inside or out is a trading-semantics call for Angus (sample includes a 10:52 winner, so strictly-before is safe).

Trigger close exactly at 09:30: the candle's data is entirely pre-market but ts.time() == anchor; ny_vwap is all-null because no NY bar has closed — flags.premarket must use strict t < anchor while the vwap-regime check tolerates null ny_vwap in the [anchor, anchor + one TF period) grace interval.
DST transition days: compare wall-clock ET extracted from the tz-aware ISO ts only (architecture invariant 2); never do offset arithmetic; do not infer anomalies from that day's unusual bar count.
Release at 07:50 with window_min = 15: the formation window completes 08:05, inside W1 — an 08:00–08:04 trigger sees a DEVELOPING extreme that must be flagged, not treated as final.

Two calendar events at the same minute (e.g. 2026-03-02 10:00 ISM Manufacturing PMI + ISM Manufacturing Prices): two data_levels rows share event_time; classify per-row, news_day derives from ANY high-impact row.
CPI day, trigger at 08:15 before the 08:30 release: data_levels is empty (or holds only stale rows) — news_day MUST be 'unknown', never 'normal'; later-today releases are invisible to the Snapshot.

Session-box gap 16:00–18:00 ET: session_of legitimately returns '' — session_label_recompute must reproduce '' rather than error; under W1 such a trigger also fails entry_window_validity (double failure is correct).
Trigger stamped Saturday, Sunday pre-18:00, or inside the 17:00–18:00 maintenance break: hard session_integrity fail — data from a closed market.

Stale data_levels: sessions.data_levels() scans the ENTIRE past calendar over the full closed frame with no expiry, so February events appear in a March snapshot; news_day must filter to current-session event_time, and the unbounded retention is flagged upstream (it also leaks stale rows into target_menu — Hephaestus lane).

Suspected CME early close (e.g. 13:00 ET day-after-Thanksgiving): W1 08:00–11:00 is technically still valid but eod_flatten and session extremes are distorted — advisory anomaly only, since no holiday input exists.

Quarterly roll week (mid Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec): front-month switch (data.py volume-based roll) can step prices vs prior-day/week levels; Snapshot carries no roll flag — advisory anomaly from date arithmetic only, clearly labeled as suspicion.
open_questions_for_spec3: MISSING SNAPSHOT FIELD (biggest): news_context — engine-computed {is_high_impact_day: bool, todays_events: [{event, impact, scheduled_ts, occurred: bool}], minutes_to_next_release, minutes_since_last_release}, derived from config/news_calendar.csv for the CURRENT CME session including not-yet-occurred events. This is NOT lookahead — the calendar is a known-ex-ante input file. Without it Helios can never emit news_day='normal' and cannot support §6.3 before the release prints, and the H4 buffer (filters.news_entry_buffer_*) is unimplementable. Agents must not read files, so the engine must surface it.

MISSING SNAPSHOT FIELD: session_integrity — {is_roll_session: bool (data.py already computes front-month change per 18:00 session), max_gap_minutes / bars_present_vs_expected in the current session, early_close: bool}. Requires adding a CME holiday/early-close calendar CSV to config/ (an input file like news_calendar.csv). Until then Helios's holiday/roll flags are labeled suspicions from LLM calendar knowledge — acceptable for the human audit trail, not for gating.
Window boundary semantics: is a candle CLOSING exactly at the window end (11:00:00 for W1) inside the window? Recommend half-open [start, end); trading-semantics call — Angus.

§9 names 'late-window entry' as a half-unit input but no threshold exists in strategy.yaml. Propose sizing.late_window_min (CALIBRATE, needs an Angus start value, e.g. final 30 min of the active window) with the standard §-traceback comment.

data_levels retention: sessions.data_levels() emits every historical calendar event with bars — no expiry. Confirm intended horizon (current session only? trailing N sessions?). Stale rows also enter Snapshot.target_menu, which touches Hephaestus's lane.

Behavior of news_day='unknown' when targets.news_day_override is enabled: note-only in the thesis, size downgrade, or veto? Recommendation: note-only (H7 §7 says news is bias/target input, not blackout) — but this is Angus's call, not engineering's.
Grace period for expecting non-null ny_vwap after the anchor: exactly one Trigger.tf period, or one 1min bar? Pin the constant in spec-3 so the check is deterministic.

Snapshot/Trigger carry no shared correlation id — timestamp string equality is the only join key. Consider adding trigger_id echoed in both (engineering; strengthens timestamp_coherence and the audit log).

Entry-window enforcement must ALSO exist deterministically in the engine/Vault path (detect_triggers start/end or a Vault time gate). Helios is cross-check (a) of the Desk's value proposition, never sole enforcement — spec-3 should state which deterministic layer owns primary window rejection so a Desk outage cannot admit out-of-window trades.

Weak § anchor for session_integrity: the constitution has no explicit holiday/roll/gap rule. Flag to Angus whether v1.1 should add a session-integrity clause (e.g. 'no entries on early-close days') or whether it stays advisory-only.
split_concerns: Four seams in the proposed split touch my lane. (1) §9 sizing composition: 'late-window entry' is a time fact (Helios) but half-unit sizing is trade construction (Hephaestus) — and specialists cannot see each other's outputs, so Hephaestus can never consume my flag. Either Hermes composes §9 from Helios.flags.late_window_entry + Atlas/Apollo confluence + Hephaestus target-R, or (recommended, cleaner) the Vault recomputes §9 deterministically and my flag is a cross-check that must agree; spec-3 must pick one and say so. (2) §6.3 news-day override: Helios owns 'is it a news day', Hephaestus owns applying the target override, but Hephaestus can't read my news_day flag. Options: Hephaestus independently re-derives day status from data_levels impacts (duplicated logic, but preserves independence and gives Hermes a consistency cross-check — I mildly favor this), or the engine's proposed news_context field is read by both lanes. (3) Pre-09:30 rule is deliberately dual-keyed: Helios owns the TIME half (ny_vwap fields null before anchor), Atlas owns the COMPOSITION half (no nyvwap_* members in the trigger's cluster) — this overlap is intentional defense-in-depth, not a gap, but spec-3 should state it explicitly so neither lane drops its half assuming the other covers it. (4) Entry-window checking overlaps the engine (detect_triggers start/end) and the Vault: fine — the Desk's stated value is independent re-derivation — but a deterministic layer must remain the primary enforcer so the Desk failing open/closed never changes window semantics. No gaps found otherwise: MTF arbitration timing (§1 shared-close resolution) is trigger anatomy and correctly sits with Apollo; data-level PRICES (are extremes in play as levels/targets) correctly sit with Atlas/Hephaestus — Helios deliberately reads only event/impact/event_time, never data_high/data_low.
